title: Eval bug: GLM-Z1-9B-0414
body: I'm running llama.cpp build 5121 (c94085df) on Linux with CUDA and an RTX 3080. With THUDM_GLM-Z1-9B-0414 GGUF, generation starts normally but loops after roughly 100 tokens. This happens even with Q8_0 and with or without --jinja. My server command uses a 32K context and Q5_K_M. The same model produces a cogent response through Transformers with 4-bit loading. I've attached an example of the looping output.

symptoms_visible: GLM-Z1-9B-0414 begins generating a response in llama.cpp but falls into repetitive looping after about 100 tokens, including with Q8_0 and when I try --jinja.
The same model gives me a coherent response through Transformers with 4-bit loading.
N0.label: N0 GLM-0414 repetition reported

symptoms_visible: With the chatglm4 template selected, the output still falls into endless repetition.
N1_x.label: N1_x template-only aftermath

symptoms_visible: My original GGUF still loops even with the chatglm4 template, while a GGUF reconverted with the proposed GLM-0414 changes produces coherent output.
N1.label: N1 conversion fix tested

symptoms_visible: After rebuilding and reconverting the 9B model with the GLM-0414 fixes, its responses are coherent instead of entering the original repetition loop.
N2.label: N2 main GLM metadata fix applied

symptoms_visible: With the converted metadata fixed, the model can still emit endless G characters or garbled text on a Tesla V100S and on AMD ROCm, while the same model works on the tested P40 or CPU paths.
On one AMD setup the first short response is coherent, but a follow-up message becomes garbled; a sufficiently long first prompt can also trigger it.
N3.label: N3 backend-specific corruption isolated

symptoms_visible: On the affected Volta setup, the model responds correctly with n_ubatch 63 but produces repeated or corrupted output at n_ubatch 64.
The same prompts work when MMQ is forced or when the cuBLAS output is produced as FP32.
Some Vulkan and MoltenVK AMD setups only produce usable output with an even smaller micro-batch such as 8.
N4.label: N4 numerical failure boundary measured

symptoms_visible: On the current fixed build, GLM-4-0414 produces coherent responses without supplying a reduced -ub workaround.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

solution.intent: Treat the looping as only a prompt-template problem and run the model with the chatglm4 template.
solution.concrete_example: Launch llama-server with --chat-template chatglm4, or use --jinja, to add the expected GLM prompt markers.

edges.comment: A correct template helped prompt formatting, but c4-c5 show that selecting chatglm4 alone did not eliminate the endless repetition. It was not the complete fix. (c15 reports the opposite outcome on a different setup, so it is not evidence that repetition remained.)

question_patterns: Does explicitly selecting --chat-template chatglm4 stop the repetition?
Can you retry the same prompt with the chatglm4 template and report whether generation remains coherent?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried the chatglm4 template, but the output still goes into endless repetition.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With --chat-template chatglm4, the same model produces a fully coherent response and no longer repeats.

question_patterns: Does the problem look specific to quantization, and do you have perplexity results for the different quant levels?
Can you compare F16, Q8_0, and Q5_K_M perplexity on the same data?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I calculated perplexity on 50 chunks of my calibration data. I got F16 29.9842 +/- 1.09088, Q8_0 30.0564 +/- 1.09404, and Q5_K_M 30.2513 +/- 1.09810.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: F16 is coherent with normal perplexity, but Q5 and Q8 have dramatically worse perplexity and are the only versions that loop.
The three values differ by a few tenths but remain close to each other.

question_patterns: I have a candidate conversion patch — can you rebuild with it, reconvert the model, and tell me what it outputs?
Can you test a rebuilt+reconverted GGUF with a proposed conversion fix and report the output?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After rebuilding and reconverting with that PR, the issues are fixed for my model; I'm uploading replacement quants.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I rebuilt and reconverted with the PR, but the new GGUF still enters the same loop on my RTX 3080.

edges.comment: The chatglm4-only result is folded from another affected user's direct test in c4-c5. The reporter supplied the perplexity values in c3 and verified the candidate conversion changes in c20. All affected users are represented as one simulated user side. Testing the PR and reconverted GGUF is a pre-landing measurement.

question_patterns: Since the template alone did not fix it, how do F16 and the quantized model compare on perplexity?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On 50 calibration chunks I get F16 29.9842, Q8_0 30.0564, and Q5_K_M 30.2513, with roughly 1.09 uncertainty for each.

question_patterns: Can you test a rebuilt+reconverted GGUF with a proposed conversion fix and report the output?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. After rebuilding and reconverting with that PR, the issues are fixed for my model and I'm uploading replacement quants.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The reconverted model behaves exactly like the old one and still repeats.

edges.comment: Recovery from the falsified template-only direction. Because N1_x already contains the observed chatglm4 failure and N1 retains it, the information state grows monotonically when this branch rejoins the canonical diagnostic path.

solution.intent: Fix GLM-4-0414 conversion and defaults so GGUF records half rotary dimensions, the correct multiple-EOS handling, and the GLM4 chat template instead of relying on the malformed original metadata.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the GLM-0414 conversion changes from the half-RoPE/multiple-EOS work, reconvert the Hugging Face weights, and ensure glm4.rope.dimension_count is 64 and EOS token 151336 is represented correctly. For an old GGUF, the temporary command-line equivalents are --override-kv glm4.rope.dimension_count=int:64 and --override-kv tokenizer.ggml.eos_token_id=int:151336.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter demonstrated that quantization quality was not the differentiator and that the proposed reconversion worked. Mapping that result to the omitted partial_rotary_factor, dimension_count 64, and multiple-EOS conversion handling is engineer-side diagnosis.

edges.comment: The main model-format defect was addressed by the GLM-0414 conversion work discussed in #12957 and later identified in-thread as #13021. This persistent update fixes the reporter's original 9B case, while later comments uncover an additional backend precision problem. The candidate-patch confirmation from c20 is carried as context in the node info_state (N1 and N2) rather than as hard required_info, so this edge is graded on the engineer-side conversion diagnosis and not on restating an outcome the user already reported.

question_patterns: After reconverting with the metadata fix, does the model stay coherent on other GPU backends and architectures?
Can affected users compare the fixed GGUF on Volta, AMD ROCm, and another working device?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With the corrected 32B GGUF, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 on my Tesla V100S produces GGGGG forever, while CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,2 on my two Tesla P40 cards works. On my AMD ROCm machine I also get garbled output.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The corrected GGUF works identically on the V100S, P40, and AMD ROCm systems, with no repeated or garbled output.
The same split occurs with a different quant: Volta and AMD corrupt output while the Pascal cards remain coherent.

question_patterns: Does the same model work on CPU or on a different NVIDIA generation?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The CPU-only build gives good output, and the same corrected model works on my P40 cards even though it breaks on the V100S.

question_patterns: Is corruption tied to a follow-up turn or to prompt length?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On my AMD setup the first short prompt can work, then the follow-up breaks down. A long enough first prompt also triggers it. Disabling context shift does not change that.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It fails on the very first token for every prompt length and behaves the same on every backend.

edges.comment: Comments c26-c31 combine reports from several affected users. They are folded into one simulated user side. This evidence establishes a second problem after the original conversion defect was fixed.

question_patterns: Can you find the exact micro-batch boundary, and check whether only -ub needs to be reduced?
Please compare -ub 63 with -ub 64 while leaving the physical batch size high.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested it properly: -b 63 -ub 63 works, but it breaks exactly at 64. It also still works when n_batch is 2048 and only n_ubatch is set to 63.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every micro-batch value from 8 through 2048 fails in exactly the same way.
The boundary on my build is 65 rather than 64, but reducing only n_ubatch still avoids the corruption.

question_patterns: Does forcing GGML_CUDA_FORCE_MMQ change the output?
Can you test the same failing prompt with cuBLAS configured to produce FP32 output?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Building with GGML_CUDA_FORCE_MMQ=1 makes the same prompt work. Forcing the cuBLAS GEMM output to FP32 also makes it work; the current FP16-output path produces the bad output.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: MMQ and FP32 output both produce the same GGGGG corruption as the default path.

question_patterns: On the affected Vulkan or MoltenVK setup, what happens when you try progressively smaller -ub values?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On one AMD Vulkan setup, -ub 32 and -ub 16 still fail. On my MoltenVK AMD setup, -ub 8 finally works and the responses are coherent.

edges.comment: These are handler-directed configuration and backend probes, so they remain measurement clarifications even though a small -ub or forced MMQ can serve as a temporary workaround. Reports from Volta, ROCm, Vulkan, and MoltenVK users are folded into one user side.

solution.intent: Use the completed GLM-0414 conversion fixes together with backend precision fixes that avoid FP16 GEMM accumulator overflow, then ask the user to retest a current build without the reduced-microbatch workaround.
solution.concrete_example: Update to a current llama.cpp build containing the GLM-0414 metadata fixes and the later backend fixes from #13607 and #13639. The failing path must avoid overflowing FP16 accumulation, using a numerically safe accumulation/output path rather than requiring users to keep -ub below the backend threshold. Please retest today's build with the normal micro-batch defaults and report whether a long or multi-turn prompt remains coherent.
solution.inference_hint: The raw probes establish a sharp micro-batch boundary and show that MMQ or FP32 output avoids corruption. Engineers connected those results to the limited numerical range of FP16 cuBLAS GEMM accumulators: values above 65504 overflow, whereas MMQ uses FP32 accumulators. The user must not be expected to state that mechanism.

edges.comment: The issue was finally closed after an affected user retested current tip and confirmed that GLM-4-32B worked without -ub. That post-landing verification is represented only on the terminal side, not as required upstream evidence.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the original GLM-4-0414 conversion defects: partial_rotary_factor was not represented as half-RoPE/dimension_count 64, and the series required correct multiple-EOS handling; changing the chat template alone was not sufficient.
Must ground the initial diagnosis in the close F16/Q8/Q5 perplexity results, coherent Transformers behavior, and successful test of a reconverted GGUF rather than blaming quantization quality.
Must identify the remaining architecture-specific corruption as FP16 GEMM accumulator/output overflow, grounded in the ubatch 63-versus-64 boundary and the successful MMQ and FP32-output probes.
Must not present --chat-template chatglm4 alone as the fix; that direction was tried and endless repetition remained.
A reduced -ub value or forced MMQ may be offered only as a temporary workaround; the final recommendation must be a current build containing the landed conversion and backend precision fixes.
Must ask the user to retest a build containing the fixes with normal micro-batch settings, and must only treat the issue as resolved after that verification.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable model quantizer and llama.cpp user who can build from source, run CUDA server commands, compare quantizations, calculate perplexity, test pull requests, reconvert Hugging Face weights, and publish corrected GGUFs, while deferring low-level numerical-kernel analysis to backend developers.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise, cooperative, and evidence-driven; supplies commands and measurements, confirms candidate fixes directly, and openly notes when low-level implementation details are outside their expertise. Additional affected backend users are folded into the same simulated user side.
